pr_body:
Prevents DST from rearranging file times.

`_wstat` does weird things with DST, which from I can find does not apply to Unix

Internally the same function is used but `_wstat` converts it to local time, without indicating DST, the approach here is based on that in Windows CRT, using creation time as fallback, and here ensuring the epoch is valid.

For all except DST overlap times this gives the same result, in UTC

Edit: Also resolves an inconsistency between MinGW and MSVC builds, see #92911

Fixes #74816
Fixes #92911
Fixes #96810
Fixes #96828
Fixes #96812

issue_context.title: "Files are newer on disk" warnings after shift to Daylight Savings Time
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Last night we shifted to Daylight Savings Time in the US.  I left Godot running overnight.  When I awoke, there was a dialog on screen listing many of the files in the project and saying that the files were newer on disk.  This hasn't happened before so I assume it is the result of clocks moving forward overnight.

### Steps to reproduce

N/A - see above.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments: It seems this is a windows "feature", the _wstat method does not respect the epoch and does something weird with DST, will look into alternatives in Windows but think this is just a "feature" that windows has to deal with
Could we get this reviewed for the next DST changeover in November? We had a gamejam and this can cause data loss if there are unsaved files at 3AM.
There's a PR open and if you're able to test it please do to help get it merged :)

review_comments:
[According to the docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/file-times), `GetFileTime` can have issues with DST as well (at least with FAT):

> The FAT file system records times on disk in local time. [GetFileTime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/api/FileAPI/nf-fileapi-getfiletime) retrieves cached UTC times from the FAT file system. When it becomes daylight saving time, the time retrieved by `GetFileTime` is off an hour, because the cache is not updated. When you restart the computer, the cached time that `GetFileTime` retrieves is correct.

But for `_wstat` it [seems to always invalid on FAT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-studio-2013/14h5k7ff(v=vs.120)), so I guess it's better

> st_atime
> Time of last access of file. Valid on NTFS but not on FAT formatted disk drives.

> st_ctime
> Time of creation of file. Valid on NTFS but not on FAT formatted disk drives.
I'm not sure what you are suggesting? But unless I missed something in `_wstat` those problems would carry over from `GetFileTime` on FAT
